title: Ravenbrook SI + SaaS integration framing
summary:
Introductory discovery between Redwood AE/SE and Ravenbrook SI team to scope potential SaaS integration and channel partnership. Discussed Ravenbrook's managed infra portfolio, target customers, security questions (VPC, KMS, SOC2), expected throughput (NLP inference at scale), and integration patterns (SDK hooks, marketplace listing vs private connector). Agreed next steps: share integration diagram, Redwood security pack, and propose pilot SLA and pricing band.
Notes: some acoustic transcription artifacts; technical numbers double-checked offline.
topics: Integration patterns: private connector vs marketplace SaaS
Performance targets and throughput (tokens/sec vs RPS)
Security: VPC, KMS, audit logs, SOC2/ISO
Pilot scope: benchmarking, pilot VMs, engineering contact matrix
next_steps: Redwood to send partner integration one-pager + security pack (Samir)
Ravenbrook to share customer archetype and expected QPS profile (Lydia)
Schedule follow-up technical deep dive with Ravenbrook infra team (Nora) - target week of Aug 30
action_items: Samir Patel | Send partner integration one-pager and security pack | 2027-08-18
Lydia Chen | Provide three customer archetypes + expected throughput (p50/p95) | 2027-08-20
Nora Kim | Setup technical deep dive calendar invite and benchmark template | 2027-08-24
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-16 14:30 PT
Duration: 46 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Nora Kim (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood), Lydia Chen (Ravenbrook), Marcus Osei (Ravenbrook), Aisha Rahman (Ravenbrook), Tom Beckett (Ravenbrook)

Auto-summary (auto): quick intro, partner fit, security questions, agree pilot next steps.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Samir from Redwood Inference, i'm the AE on this APAC-west partnership motion. real quick intros?
[00:09] Lydia: hi Samir, Lydia here, head of platform at Ravenbrook, we do managed inference stacks for mid-market healthcare and financials, we also have a small SI arm for custom integrations.
[00:18] Marcus: Marcus Osei, CTO, i mostly focus on infra and ops.
[00:21] Samir: great. Nora, you wanna intro?
[00:24] Nora: yeah Nora Kim, SE, i'll be the technical lead for any proofs and benchmarks, happy to dig into runtimes and perf.
[00:31] Tom: Tom Beckett, partnerships, we'll be owning GTM collaboration.
[00:35] Diego: diego alivarez, solutions eng on redwood, coming from the runtime side.
[00:38] Aisha: Aisha here, solutions architect, i'll be the day-to-day eng contact from ravenbrook for integration work.

[02:05] Samir: goal for today is pretty simple, understand Ravenbrook's integration model — when you say managed inference stack, are you mainly offering a hosted SaaS for customers or an SI kit they embed on-prem? or both? and see where Redwood might slot in as a model host or distro partner.
[02:23] Lydia: mostly both. our bread-and-butter is a managed SaaS offering that runs in our cloud tenancy for customers that want hands-off. For more regulated clients we do a private package, customer-managed VPC or on-prem. we want to surface a marketplace connector too, like list our offering so customers can click-to-deploy.
[02:45] Marcus: there are two technical constraints for us: one is data residency, many customers need in-EU or in-region hosting; two is throughput. we see peaks up to 5000 RPS for embedding workloads — though those are bursty — and sustained gen workloads of ~300 tokens/sec aggregated for some customers.
[03:10] Nora: just to clarify, when you say 5000 RPS for embeddings, is that per tenant or total?
[03:15] Marcus: usually per customer cluster during business hours. it's often fronted by a vector db cache but still a lot.

[04:02] Samir: ok that's helpful. two integration patterns we typically recommend: one, a private connector / VPC peering model (good for enterprise customers who need a private control plane and KMS integration), and two, a marketplace listing where you bundle a Redwood-hosted runtime as a managed model endpoint that you can white-label. both have trade-offs.
[04:25] Aisha: trade-offs like latency vs control right? marketplace is simpler for GTM but customers lose some network isolation.
[04:30] Samir: correct. marketplace is fastest to onboard — you get a hosted API endpoint — but for high-security customers you likely want dedicated or private deployment (VPC + bring-your-own-KMS).

[05:12] Nora: on the runtime side we do a lot of continuous batching and kv cache optimizations. Diego, do you want to explain how we handle quantized models and kernel selection?
[05:20] Diego: sure. our serving runtime is optimized for attention kernels and supports int8 / q4 quant paths. we also do adaptive batching based on sequence length histograms. for an SI integration we can expose a lightweight SDK that does token-rate throttling and per-tenant KV prefixes to reduce redundant compute.
[05:45] Marcus: are there any open source pieces required on our side? we try to minimize vendor lock for our customers.
[05:50] Diego: you can run either way, we have a small agent for private deployments (thin proxy + mTLS) that only needs a small outbound to control plane. if you want fully air-gapped we can produce an on-prem package but that adds lead time.

[07:12] Lydia: security is big for our financial customers. do you have SOC2 and ISO attestation? and how do you handle key management?
[07:20] Samir: yes SOC2 type II, and we have ISO 27001 — i'll share our compliance pack. for KMS you can use customer-managed keys in the VPC/private model; hosted model uses our KMS but we support bring-your-own-key via HSM integrations for enterprise plans.
[07:45] Aisha: audit logs? we need full request/response audit for certain customers, and retention controls per jurisdiction.
[07:52] Nora: Redwood's console exposes token-level traces, per-route logs, and you can forward audit streams to your SIEM (we support s3 sinks and direct syslog). retention tiers are configurable under our enterprise SLA.

[09:05] Marcus: performance: do you support GPU pooling / reserved capacity? and how deterministic is latency at p95?
[09:12] Samir: yes we have dedicated pools (reserved) and we can carve out GPU pools per partner. typical p95 for 2048 tokens on a tuned model is in the 120-220ms range on A100-equivalent instances in our hosted tier; dedicated tends to be tighter. we'll caveat that it depends on model size and quantization.
[09:40] Marcus: can you run benchmarks with our sequence lengths? we need to compare memory/kv cache behavior.
[09:45] Nora: absolutely — we'll send a benchmark template and can run a joint run on a partner-dedicated node or provide the runner to you.

[11:05] Tom: on GTM, Ravenbrook wants to list a vetted connector in our marketplace and co-sponsor webinars for joint customers. we also want a revenue share discussion.
[11:12] Samir: sounds good; we typically do revenue share for partners who bring consistent consumption. we also offer co-marketing credits for the first quarter. we'll have our partner lead draft terms.

[12:34] Aisha: technical detail — how do you handle model rollouts and fallback policies? some of our customers want canary deploys to a smaller segment and fail back to a cheaper model if a perf regression occurs.
[12:44] Diego: Redwood supports canary and A/B rollouts per route, with automatic fallback to a compatible variant. the scheduler can route by policy: latency, cost, region. it also supports prefix/KV cache warming so canaries don't thrash the cache.

[14:10] Marcus: network topology: for private model hosting, do you support VPC peering and private link style connectivity?
[14:16] Nora: yes we support VPC peering, private link, and direct connect equivalents. for on-prem we support a reverse-tunnel agent that opens an outbound TLS channel to our control plane; we avoid inbound rules to reduce attack surface.

[16:55] Lydia: ok budget and licensing — we sell managed infra as part of our packages. what are typical pricing bands for dedicated capacity vs hosted?
[17:05] Samir: pricing depends on reserved GPU months, model size, and egress. ballpark: hosted per-token and per-embedding units; dedicated reserved monthly starts with a minimum commit (we'll provide ranges). for partner pilots we can do a limited trial with usage credit. we'll follow up with pricing bands in the partner one-pager.

[20:00] Marcus: PII concerns — some customers require redaction before leaving the tenant boundary. do you have pre-send redaction hooks?
[20:07] Diego: yes we support pre-request transformers, you can run pre-send redaction or client-side anonymization. for private deployments you can enforce local-only transforms.

[22:34] Aisha: about observability, do you provide token-level cost attribution per request? we want to map usage to our customers for billing.
[22:40] Nora: yes, our billing and observability expose token counts and per-route cost breakdown. we also provide trace IDs to correlate logs and to push metrics to datadog or prometheus endpoints.

[25:00] Samir: ok let's sketch the pilot scope — two customers: one mid-market EU bank for private deployment (on-prem or VPC) focusing on redaction + audit logs; second is a US SaaS customer that will use marketplace hosted endpoint for embeddings at high RPS. idea is to validate throughput, security, and GTM packaging.
[25:20] Lydia: that seems reasonable. timeline: Ravenbrook wants to pilot in Q4. we need results before end of quarter.

[27:10] Nora: technical deep dive plan: step 1 send benchmark template and network diagram; step 2 run synthetic load for embeddings and gen; step 3 produce p50/p95 numbers and cache hit rates. we'll also do an SLO table.

[30:45] Marcus: who will be the escalation contact on Redwood? we need an SE and an account lead.
[30:50] Samir: SE is Nora; Diego will be the runtime lead for the bench. alex shaun is our partner lead for legal/commercial — i'll include them on the follow-up.

[33:12] Tom: legal — we need basic MSSP language for the connector and a marketplace listing contract template. can you share a template?
[33:20] Samir: yes, we'll share a starter MSA and the marketplace terms. legal will redline; revenue share and liability bands will be in that doc.

[36:00] Aisha: small nit — our support model expects a runbook for failover. do you provide runbooks or SRE handoff docs?
[36:07] Diego: yes we do an SRE handoff including runbooks, playbooks for cache eviction, scaling ops, and per-tenant debugging guides.

[38:50] Lydia: anything we should be cautious about?
[38:54] Nora: some of the transcription i saw earlier said 'kay vee cash' — that's kv cache. also note quantization can change accuracy; we'll include guidance on regen callbacks and evals.

[40:12] Marcus: final ask: can Redwood commit to a partner-dedicated node for the pilot window? we want isolated capacity for predictable numbers.
[40:20] Samir: yes we can provision a partner-dedicated node for the pilot. we'll put a minimal reserved commit for the test window; details in the partner one-pager.

[42:00] Samir: quick recap: Redwood to send partner integration one-pager, compliance pack, benchmark template; Ravenbrook to share customer archetypes and QPS profiles; schedule technical deep dive with infra team. target dates noted.
[42:18] Lydia: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[42:22] Tom: appreciate the quick sync.
[42:30] Samir: i'll follow up with calendar invites and send the security docs. thanks all.

[45:00] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-attribution and ASR errors on acronyms (e.g., KV -> "kay vee"), some speaker pauses removed. For exact performance numbers refer to Nora's benchmark template and the follow-up technical deep dive recording.
